## Analysis

**Top Tc samples in the dataset:**

| Composition | Tc (K) |
|---|---|
| H2S1 | 185.0 |
| Hg1Ba2Ca2Cu3O8 | 132.0 |
| Ba2Ca2Cu3O | 126.0 |
| Tl0.5Pb0.5Ba1.6Sr0.4Ca2Cu3O | 120.2 |
| Tl1Ba1Ca1Cu2O5.5 | 114.0 |
| Bi2Sr2Ca1Cu2O10 | 110.0 |

Key observations:
- The record holder (H2S1) uses hydrogen and sulfur — **not available** in the design variables.
- Hg1Ba2Ca2Cu3O8 (132 K) uses Hg — also **not available**.
- The best achievable family is the **Ba–Ca–Cu–O cuprates**: the sample **Ba2Ca2Cu3O (126 K)** uses exactly the 4 allowed elements Ba, Ca, Cu, O — the Hg-free analogue of Hg-1223, with triple CuO₂ planes separated by Ca, and Ba charge reservoir layers.
- The trend in the data is clear: multi-layer cuprates (2–3 CuO₂ planes) with Ba/Ca spacers dominate the top of the Tc range (105–132 K), far above single-layer or Sr-substituted variants.

**Proposed stoichiometry:** Ba₂Ca₂Cu₃O₈ (the full oxygen content of the 1223-type structure), total atoms = 15:
- Ba = 2/15 = 0.133333 (≤ 0.333333 ✓)
- Ca = 2/15 = 0.133333 (≤ 0.272727 ✓)
- Cu = 3/15 = 0.200000 (≤ 0.454545 ✓)
- O = 8/15 = 0.533333 (≤ 0.697674 ✓)

This uses exactly 4 elements, all within bounds, and matches the highest-Tc composition realizable with the allowed element set (~126 K observed).

Final: O=0.533333, Cu=0.200000, Ba=0.133333, Ca=0.133333
